name: Manasseh
bio:
Manasseh succeeded his father Hezekiah as king of Judah after Hezekiah's death (2 Kings 20:21).

## 📖 Core Story: Judah's Worst King

Manasseh became king at twelve and reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem, longer than any other king of Judah; his mother was Hephzibah. He rebuilt the high places his father Hezekiah had destroyed, raised altars to Baal, made an Asherah pole like Ahab had, worshipped the heavenly host, built pagan altars in the LORD's own temple courts, made his son pass through fire, and practiced divination, sorcery, and necromancy — doing more evil than the nations the LORD had driven out before Israel. He even set up an Asherah image in the temple itself, the very house where the LORD had promised to put his name forever, and led Judah to sin even more than Israel had. Through the prophets, the LORD declared that because of Manasseh's abominations and the innocent blood he shed throughout Jerusalem, he would bring such disaster on Jerusalem and Judah that it would be wiped out like a dish and handed over to its enemies as plunder. Manasseh died and was buried in the garden of his own house, the garden of Uzza; his son Amon succeeded him (2 Kings 21:1-18).
